explanation: When a fact describes its own entity, storing it once there avoids repeating the same data across many related rows. The customer city belongs with the customer, while invoices can point to that customer.

options.text: Keep the city only in the customer table and reference the customer from each invoice
Duplicate the city in every invoice row so queries are faster
Replace the customer identifier with the customer city
Store the city once per invoice line item and once per invoice header

prompt: A sales app stores each invoice with the customer’s city in every invoice row. If the customer moves, many old rows would need updates. Which design choice best reduces this redundancy?
reviewConcept: Move repeated facts to the entity they describe.
